newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Russia '96/97 grain exports to be low.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Russia '96/97 grain exports to be low.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA'S 1996-1997 GRAIN EXPORTS SEEN AT 0.6-0.8 MILLION TONNES, CLOSE TO 1995-1996'S LOW LEVELS

MOSCOW, Sept 12 - In contrast to official forecasts that Russia will export 3-4 million tonnes of grain in 1996-1997, SovEcon predicts Russian exports will be similar to 1995-1996 levels, at about 0.6-0.8 million tonnes.
In the 1995-1996 crop year, Russia's total grain exports fell sharply to 0.7 million tonnes, compared to 3 million tonnes in 1994-1995.
There were particular declines in barley and wheat exports.
As a result, Russia became a net importer of all main grains in 1995/1996, including barley and rye, reflecting the serious decline in last year's grain output, the lowest in the last thirty years.

SovEcon's current forecast for Russia's total 1996 grain output is now about 70 million tonnes. That is 11 percent above last year's drought-reduced level, but this year's harvest will still be the third-lowest in the last three decades.
Russia's low harvest this year is exacerbated by a serious fall in grain stocks.
Last year's bad harvest was mainly offset by drawing upon central and farm stocks.
But by July 1, 1996, total farm grain stocks had declined to 2.9 million tonnes, which was 2.3 million tonnes below July 1995's level.
Stocks of all major grains were significantly lower than last year, particularly of barley (nearly three times down on year-ago levels) and of rye (down 2.5 times).
In addition, there was a drastic decline in total state carry-overs -- by July 1, 1996, they had been virtually depleted, against 8.8 million metric tonnes at the same date last year.
Very tight supplies severely limit Russia's export potential for 1996-1997.
Barley exports are forecast at about 0.2-0.3 million tonnes and wheat exports (including flour) 0.3-0.4 million tonnes.
This trend has been confirmed to a certain extent by negligible exports in July, which is the beginning of the 1996-1997 crop season.
